encoding.name: 128B
encoding.semantics: 128 bytes per transfer. The size of any transfer must not exceed the data bus width of either agent.

encoding.name: FIXED
encoding.semantics: Address is the same for every transfer in the burst; valid byte lanes constant. Used for repeated accesses to the same location, e.g. FIFO load/empty.

encoding.name: INCR
encoding.semantics: Incrementing — address for each transfer in the burst is an increment of the previous address. Increment value depends on AxSIZE. Used for accesses to normal sequential memory.

encoding.name: WRAP
encoding.semantics: Wrapping — like INCR, but address wraps around to a lower address (the wrap boundary) when an upper limit is reached. Start address must be aligned to AxSIZE; burst length must be 2, 4, 8, or 16. Used for cache line accesses.

encoding.name: OKAY
encoding.semantics: Normal access success; or failure of an exclusive access; or exclusive access to a slave that does not support exclusive access. Default response.

encoding.name: EXOKAY
encoding.semantics: Exclusive access okay — success of an exclusive read or write. Only legal as a response to an exclusive transaction.

encoding.name: SLVERR
encoding.semantics: Slave error — access reached the slave successfully but the slave returns an error (e.g. FIFO overrun/underrun, unsupported size, write to read-only, slave timeout, access to disabled function).

encoding.name: DECERR
encoding.semantics: Decode error — typically generated by an interconnect to indicate that there is no slave at the transaction address. The interconnect should route to a default slave that returns DECERR.

encoding.name: Exclusive access
encoding.semantics: Exclusive access — selects exclusive read/write monitoring.

encoding.name: Locked access
encoding.semantics: Locked access — interconnect must ensure only this master can access the targeted slave region until an unlocked transaction from the same master completes. Removed in AXI4.

encoding.name: Exclusive access
encoding.semantics: Exclusive access — selects exclusive read/write monitoring. Locked access is removed in AXI4.

encoding.name: Non-bufferable
encoding.semantics: Bufferable (B) bit deasserted — transaction must NOT be delayed by the interconnect.

encoding.name: Bufferable
encoding.semantics: Bufferable (B) bit asserted — interconnect or any component can delay the transaction reaching its final destination for any number of cycles. Normally only relevant to writes.

encoding.name: Non-cacheable
encoding.semantics: Cacheable (C) bit deasserted — allocation of the transaction is forbidden.

encoding.name: Cacheable
encoding.semantics: Cacheable (C) bit asserted — allocation permitted; characteristics at final destination need not match the original.

encoding.name: Read-Allocate
encoding.semantics: RA bit asserted — must not be set if C bit deasserted.

encoding.name: Write-Allocate
encoding.semantics: WA bit asserted — must not be set if C bit deasserted.

encoding.name: Allocate
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction must be looked up in cache (could have been previously allocated); recommended to be allocated. When deasserted (and [2] deasserted), no lookup required, must propagate to final destination.

encoding.name: Other Allocate
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction must be looked up in cache (could have been allocated by another transaction/master). When deasserted (and [3] deasserted), no lookup required.

encoding.name: Modifiable
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction characteristics can be modified and writes can be merged. When deasserted, characteristics must not be modified.

encoding.name: Bufferable
encoding.semantics: When deasserted with [3:2] deasserted, write response must come from final destination. When asserted with [3:2] deasserted, response can come from intermediate point but write must be made visible at final destination in a timely manner. With [3:2] asserted, response can come from intermediate point.

encoding.name: Other Allocate
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction must be looked up in cache (could have been allocated by a write transaction or another master). When deasserted (and [2] deasserted), no lookup required.

encoding.name: Allocate
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction must be looked up in cache (could have been allocated); recommended to be allocated.

encoding.name: Modifiable
encoding.semantics: When asserted, characteristics can be modified and a larger quantity of read data can be fetched than required.

encoding.name: Bufferable
encoding.semantics: No effect if [3:1] deasserted. With [3:2] deasserted and [1] asserted: deasserted -> read data must come from final destination; asserted -> can come from final destination or a write progressing to it. When [3] or [2] asserted, distinguishes Write-Through vs Write-Back.

tables.name: AXI4 Memory type encoding (ARCACHE / AWCACHE -> memory type)

encoding.name: Device Non-bufferable
encoding.semantics: Write response from final destination; read data from final destination; Non-modifiable; no prefetch; no merging.

encoding.name: Device Bufferable
encoding.semantics: Write response can be intermediate; writes visible at final destination in a timely manner; reads from final destination; Non-modifiable; no prefetch; no merging.

encoding.name: Reserved
encoding.semantics: All values not shown in Table A4-5 are reserved.

encoding.name: Secure access
encoding.semantics: Secure address space (note: signal is asserted-LOW for Secure — bit value 0 == Secure).

encoding.name: Data access
encoding.semantics: Data access (recommended default unless instruction access is known).

encoding.name: Instruction access
encoding.semantics: Instruction access. AXI defines this as a hint; not accurate when a transaction contains a mix of instruction and data items.

encoding.name: Address
encoding.semantics: Must not be changed by interconnect when transaction is Non-modifiable.

encoding.name: Burst length
encoding.semantics: Must not be changed (AXI4 INCR>16 may be split, see A4.3).

encoding.name: WID (AXI3 only)
encoding.semantics: Write data channel ID; removed in AXI4.

encoding.name: BID
encoding.semantics: Write response channel ID — must match the AWID of the transaction being responded to.

encoding.name: RID
encoding.semantics: Read data channel ID — slave must ensure RID matches the ARID of the address it is responding to.

burst_address_equations.WRAP_wrap_condition: If Address_N = Wrap_Boundary + Number_Bytes*Burst_Length then Address_N := Wrap_Boundary

evidence.quote: Table A3-2 Burst size encoding: 0b000=1, 0b001=2, 0b010=4, 0b011=8, 0b100=16, 0b101=32, 0b110=64, 0b111=128 bytes in transfer.
Table A3-3 Burst type encoding: AxBURST 0b00=FIXED, 0b01=INCR, 0b10=WRAP, 0b11=Reserved.

evidence.spec_section: A3.4 Read and write response structure

evidence.quote: Table A4-1: AxCACHE[0] Bufferable, [1] Cacheable, [2] Read-Allocate, [3] Write-Allocate.
Table A4-3 / Table A4-4: AWCACHE = {Allocate, Other Allocate, Modifiable, Bufferable}; ARCACHE = {Other Allocate, Allocate, Modifiable, Bufferable}.
Table A4-5: ARCACHE/AWCACHE encodings -> Device Non-bufferable through Write-Back Read and Write-Allocate. All values not shown are reserved.
Table A4-6 AxPROT[2:0]: [0] Unprivileged/Privileged, [1] Secure/Non-secure, [2] Data/Instruction.
Table A7-1 AXI3 AxLOCK[1:0]: 0b00 Normal, 0b01 Exclusive, 0b10 Locked, 0b11 Reserved. Table A7-2 AXI4 AxLOCK 1-bit: 0b0 Normal, 0b1 Exclusive.
AW->AWID, W (AXI3 only)->WID, B->BID, AR->ARID, R->RID.
